newsitem.title: USA: Damark sees Q2, 1997 above expectations.
newsitem.headline: Damark sees Q2, 1997 above expectations.

text.p: Damark International Inc said it it expects revenues and earnings to exceed analysts' expectations for the second quarter ending June 28 and for the full year ending December 31.

The direct marketing company said it estimates revenues for the second quarter will top year-ago revenues by 15 to 17 percent. The company said it expects quarterly earnings per share improvement of twice the revenue growth rate.
"Damark also expects the second half of 1997 to continue to reflect improved operating results," it said.
Damark expects to report second-quarter results during the third week of July.

"Damark is now positioned to grow more rapidly, a result of our two-year effort to reposition our core catalog business by focusing on customer satisfaction, reducing costs, improving product and catalog profitability and building an infrastructure to support future growth," said chairman and chief executive Mark Cohn.
"We are particularly pleased with the revenue growth from this part of our business, where sales per catalog mailed are rising," he said.

"Additionally, the strategically critical expansion of our membership services business is contributing to our ability to grow earnings at a faster rate than revenue growth. During 1997 we will continue to develop new club concepts and further third party marketing partnerships," Cohn added.
Damark posted second-quarter 1996 net revenues of $124.1 million and earnings per share of $0.17 and full year 1996 net revenues of $513.7 million and earnings per share of $0.70.
